instruction:
Load /home/user/Desktop/p1.step, /home/user/Desktop/p2.step, and /home/user/Desktop/p3.step in FreeCAD 0.21.2 Path/CAM. To use FreeCAD, run `freecad` from a terminal (use the full executable path if it is not on PATH). On this machine, use `/usr/lib/freecad/bin/freecadcmd-python3` for FreeCAD Path command-line automation when working on `p1.step`.

Treat each STEP independently and create one separate Job for each part; each Job must contain only its corresponding part and exactly one active outside Profile operation. Each imported part is a 120 x 80 x 18 mm block with source bounds X=-60..60, Y=-40..40, and Z=0..18 mm. Use zero stock extension so each Job stock matches its part. Set each Job's G54 origin to that part's top-face center at source (0, 0, 18), so the posted work coordinates have the top at Z=0 and the bottom at Z=-18. Use T1 with the same practical flat end-mill definition in all three Jobs, clockwise spindle S7000 rpm, and horizontal cutting feed F500 mm/min. Profile the complete outside perimeter down to Z=-18 without cutting below it, with a positive StepDown and safe and clearance heights above Z=0. Use FreeCAD's LinuxCNC postprocessor. Save each native Job and its posted program at exactly /home/user/Desktop/p1.FCStd and /home/user/Desktop/p1.nc, /home/user/Desktop/p2.FCStd and /home/user/Desktop/p2.nc, and /home/user/Desktop/p3.FCStd and /home/user/Desktop/p3.nc.
